KE.name: NSSF Tier I + Tier II employer contribution (6 % of pensionable earnings up to the Upper Earnings Limit)
KE.statute: National Social Security Fund Act 2013 (Cap. 258) s. 20, Third Schedule (Table: year 2 UEL = 1 × National Average Earnings, year 3 LEL 8 000 / UEL = 2 × NAE); year 3 runs from February 2025
KE.doc: s. 20: the employer pays Tier I contributions (6 % of earnings up to the Lower Earnings Limit) and Tier II contributions (6 % of earnings between the LEL and the Upper Earnings Limit), matching the employee; pensionable earnings are the lower of monthly wages and the UEL. Third Schedule: year 2 (February 2024 - January 2025) UEL = 1 × NAE, year 3 (February 2025 - January 2026) UEL = 2 × NAE. NAE = 36 000 Kshs, inferred from the NSSF year-4 notice (UEL 108 000 = 3 × NAE) — the year-3 notice itself is not held. For 2025: January at 6 % of up to 36 000, February-December at 6 % of up to 72 000, i.e. an annual ceiling of 36 000 + 11 × 72 000 = 828 000 per employee.
unsupported: the annual ceiling is exact for constant monthly wages up to 36 000 or from 69 000; in between the January month is slightly over-counted

RW.name: Maternity leave benefits scheme, employer share (0,3 % of gross salary)
RW.statute: Law n° 003/2016 establishing and governing maternity leave benefits scheme (Official Gazette n° Special of 20/04/2016) art. 6-7; Law n° 049/2024 of 04/06/2024 amends registration, audit, benefit calculation, payment and reimbursement, not the rate of art. 7
RW.doc: art. 6: contributions are based on the gross salary; art. 7: the contribution is 0,6 % of the salary, the employer and the employee each paying 0,3 %.

RW.name: Occupational hazards scheme (employer contribution)
RW.why: the instrument fixing the occupational-hazards contribution rate is not held (Law 05/2015 governs pensions only; art. 8 there is the pension rate)
